title.zh: 卷248 列傳三十五 许定国 左梦庚 田雄 张天禄 孙可望
title.en: Volume 248 Biographies 35: Xu Dingguo, Zuo Menggeng, Tian Xiong, Zhang Tianlu, Sun Kewang
title.raw: 卷248 列傳三十五 许定国 左梦庚 田雄 张天禄 孙可望

sentences.zh: 列傳三十五

translations.literal: Biographies 35
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 35

sentences.zh: =許定國=許定國，河南太康人。

translations.literal: Xu Dingguo: Xu Dingguo was a native of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dingguo was a native of Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎間，官山西總兵官。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he served as regional commander of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he held the post of regional commander of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 李自成圍開封，趣定國赴援，師次沁水，一夕師潰，逮治論死。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng, [the court] urged Dingguo to relieve the city; his army halted at Qinshui; in a single night the army collapsed; he was arrested and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng, the court ordered Dingguo to march to the relief of the city. His army halted at Qinshui, and in the course of a single night it disintegrated. He was taken into custody and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 尋复授援剿河南總兵官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again appointed regional commander for relief and suppression in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed regional commander charged with relieving and suppressing rebellion in Henan.

sentences.zh: 福王時，駐軍睢州。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, he garrisoned his troops at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he garrisoned his forces at Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，豫親王多鐸下河南，次孟津，定國使請降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Prince Yu Dodo advanced into Henan and encamped at Mengjin; Dingguo sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, Prince Yu Dodo led his army into Henan and halted at Mengjin. Dingguo dispatched envoys to offer his surrender.

sentences.zh: 肅親王豪格略山東，复上書請以其孥來附，肅親王命遣子為質。

translations.literal: When Prince Su Haoge campaigned in Shandong, [Dingguo] again wrote requesting to bring his wife and children to submit; Prince Su ordered him to send his son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Su Haoge was campaigning in Shandong, Dingguo wrote again asking permission to bring his family and submit. Prince Su ordered him to send his son as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣其子詣肅親王軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he sent his son to Prince Su's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent his son to join Prince Su's army as hostage.

sentences.zh: 明督師大學士史可法遣總兵高傑徇河南，次歸德，聞定國已遣子納款，招往會，不赴。

translations.literal: The Ming Grand Secretary and supreme commander Shi Kefa dispatched Regional Commander Gao Jie to campaign in Henan; Jie encamped at Guide; hearing that Dingguo had already sent his son to surrender, he invited him to a meeting, but [Dingguo] did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Grand Secretary and supreme commander Shi Kefa sent Regional Commander Gao Jie to advance through Henan. Jie halted at Guide. When he learned that Dingguo had already sent his son to tender surrender, he summoned Dingguo to a meeting, but Dingguo refused to come.

sentences.zh: 傑乃與巡撫越其傑、巡按陳潛夫就定國睢州，定國不得已郊迎。

translations.literal: Jie then went with Governor Yue Qijie and Censor Chen Qianfu to Dingguo's [base at] Suizhou; Dingguo had no choice but to go out to the suburbs to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then went with Governor Yue Qijie and Investigating Censor Chen Qianfu to Dingguo's headquarters at Suizhou. Dingguo had no choice but to go out beyond the walls to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其傑勸傑勿入城，傑輕定國，不聽。

translations.literal: Qijie urged Jie not to enter the city; Jie looked down on Dingguo and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie urged Jie not to enter the city, but Jie held Dingguo in contempt and would not heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 既入，定國宴傑，侑以妓。

translations.literal: Once inside, Dingguo feasted Jie and entertained him with courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jie had entered the city, Dingguo held a banquet for him and provided courtesans to enliven the feast.

sentences.zh: 傑酣，為定國刻行期，並微及遣子納款事。

translations.literal: When Jie was drunk, he fixed a date for Dingguo to depart and subtly mentioned the matter of sending his son to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie was deep in his cups, he set a date for Dingguo to take the field and obliquely brought up the matter of his son's surrender.

sentences.zh: 定國益懼，中夜伏兵殺傑。

translations.literal: Dingguo grew still more fearful; in the middle of the night he ambushed and killed Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo grew still more afraid. In the middle of the night he set an ambush and killed Jie.

sentences.zh: 明日，傑部將攻定國屠城。

translations.literal: The next day Jie's subordinate generals attacked Dingguo and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jie's subordinate commanders attacked Dingguo and put the city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 定國走考城，遂來降。

translations.literal: Dingguo fled to Kaocheng, then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo fled to Kaocheng and then came over to the Qing side.

sentences.zh: 豫親王請以定國從征，留其孥曹縣，命河道總督楊方興厚贍之。

translations.literal: Prince Yu requested that Dingguo accompany the campaign; his wife and children were left at Caoxian; River Conservancy Director Yang Fangxing was ordered to provide for them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu asked that Dingguo accompany the army on campaign. His family was left at Caoxian, and River Conservancy Director Yang Fangxing was ordered to support them generously.

sentences.zh: 定國妻邢有疾，乞還鄉里，方興為代奏。

translations.literal: Dingguo's wife the Lady Xing was ill; she begged to return to her native place; Fangxing memorialized on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo's wife, née Xing, fell ill and begged to return to her home district. Fangxing submitted a memorial on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 命暫居曹縣，俟定國入覲。

translations.literal: [The throne] ordered her to stay temporarily at Caoxian until Dingguo came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: She was ordered to remain temporarily at Caoxian until Dingguo should come to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師還，定國詣京師，隸漢軍鑲白旗。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu's army returned, Dingguo went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered White Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army returned, Dingguo went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered White Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died.

sentences.zh: 五年，以來降功，授一等精奇尼哈番，子爾安襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for merit in surrendering, [the line] was granted the first-rank jingqi niha; his son Er'an inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, in recognition of his merit in coming over to the Qing, the family was granted a first-rank jingqi niha banner rank. His son Er'an inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔求言，爾安為睿親王多爾袞訟功德，請修其墓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when an edict solicited opinion, Er'an pleaded the merit and virtue of Prince Regent Dorgon and requested repair of his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when an edict called for memorials offering counsel, Er'an pleaded the merits and virtues of Prince Regent Dorgon and asked that his tomb be restored.

sentences.zh: 語詳睿親王傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of Prince Regent Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 坐煽惑，減死流寧古塔。

translations.literal: For the crime of incitement, his death sentence was reduced to exile at Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of incitement, he was spared execution and banished to Ningguta instead.

sentences.zh: 弟爾吉襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Erji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Erji inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 史可法置江北四鎮，傑與劉澤清、劉良佐、黃得功分領之。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa established the four garrisons north of the Yangtze; Jie together with Liu Zeqing, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong each commanded one.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa established the four garrisons north of the Yangtze, which Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong were to command respectively.

sentences.zh: 傑為定國所殺，得功戰死蕪湖。

translations.literal: Jie was killed by Dingguo; Degong died in battle at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was killed by Dingguo, and Degong fell in battle at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 劉良佐，直隸人，明總兵，預擁立福王。

translations.literal: Liu Liangzuo, a native of Zhili, was a Ming regional commander and had taken part in enthroning the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liangzuo, a native of Zhili, had been a Ming regional commander and had taken part in raising the Prince of Fu to the throne.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，豫親王下江南，良佐以兵十萬來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when Prince Yu advanced into Jiangnan, Liangzuo came to surrender with an army of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, when Prince Yu marched into Jiangnan, Liangzuo surrendered with a force of one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 江南定，詣京師，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, he went to the capital and was enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，以來降功，授世職二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for merit in surrendering, he was granted the hereditary second-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, for his merit in surrendering, he was granted a hereditary second-rank jingqi niha banner rank.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍譚泰討金聲桓。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Tan Tai in campaigning against Jin Shengheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Tan Tai in the campaign against Jin Shengheng.

sentences.zh: 師還，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed a minister of honorific rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed a minister of honorific rank.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授江南江安提督，加總管銜。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Jiang'an provincial military commander of Jiangnan, with the additional title of superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Jiang'an provincial military commander in Jiangnan and given the additional title of superintendent.

sentences.zh: 尋改直隸提督，改左都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhili and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to provincial military commander of Zhili and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kangxi he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 劉澤清既降复叛，誅死。

translations.literal: Liu Zeqing, having surrendered, rebelled again and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeqing, having surrendered and then rebelled again, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 左夢庚，山東臨清人。

translations.literal: Zuo Menggeng was a native of Linqing in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Menggeng was a native of Linqing in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父良玉，明史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Liangyu has a biography in the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo Liangyu has a biography in the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 良玉初授平賊將軍，及封寧南伯，以平賊將軍印授夢庚。

translations.literal: Liangyu was first appointed General for Pacifying Bandits; when he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningnan, he gave the seal of General for Pacifying Bandits to Menggeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu was first appointed General for Pacifying Bandits, and when he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningnan he transferred the seal of that office to Menggeng.

sentences.zh: 福王時，良玉舉兵自武昌東下，號「清君側」。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Liangyu raised troops and marched east from Wuchang under the slogan "Clear the emperor's side."
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Liangyu raised an army and marched east from Wuchang under the slogan of clearing away evil ministers at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 次九江，病卒。

translations.literal: He halted at Jiujiang and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Jiujiang, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 諸將推夢庚為帥。

translations.literal: The generals acclaimed Menggeng as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The generals acclaimed Menggeng as their commander.

sentences.zh: 總督袁繼咸禦戰，夢庚還駐池州，遣兵間道自彭澤下建德，遂取安慶。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yuan Jixian resisted in battle; Menggeng withdrew to garrison at Chizhou, sent troops by a secret route from Pengze down to Jiande, and thus took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yuan Jixian met them in battle. Menggeng withdrew to Chizhou, then sent troops by a hidden route from Pengze down toward Jiande and seized Anqing.

sentences.zh: 總兵黃得功破之銅陵，乃退保九江。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Huang Degong defeated him at Tongling; he then withdrew to hold Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Huang Degong defeated him at Tongling, and he withdrew to defend Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，英親王阿濟格逐李自成至九江，夢庚率眾降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Ying Ajige pursued Li Zicheng to Jiujiang; Menggeng led his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, Prince Ying Ajige pursued Li Zicheng as far as Jiujiang. Menggeng led his forces in surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，入覲，宴午門內，命隸漢軍正黃旗。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he came to audience; a banquet was held inside the Meridian Gate; he was ordered enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he came to court for an audience and was feasted inside the Meridian Gate. He was enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「部將盧光祖、李國英從入京師，餘若張應祥、徐恩盛、郝效忠、金聲桓、常登、徐勇、吳學禮、張應元、徐育賢俱奉英親王調發防剿江西、湖廣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "My subordinate generals Lu Guangzu and Li Guoying accompanied [me] into the capital; the rest, such as Zhang Yingxiang, Xu Ensheng, Hao Xiaozhong, Jin Shengheng, Chang Deng, Xu Yong, Wu Xueli, Zhang Yingyuan, and Xu Yuxian, were all dispatched by Prince Ying for defense and suppression in Jiangxi and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "My subordinate commanders Lu Guangzu and Li Guoying accompanied me to the capital. The rest—Zhang Yingxiang, Xu Ensheng, Hao Xiaozhong, Jin Shengheng, Chang Deng, Xu Yong, Wu Xueli, Zhang Yingyuan, and Xu Yuxian among them—have all been assigned by Prince Ying to garrison and suppress rebellion in Jiangxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 誠恐諸將在外，踪跡未定，室家未安，訛惑之事，不可不籌。」

translations.literal: I truly fear that with the generals abroad, their whereabouts unsettled and their families not yet secure, matters of rumor and confusion cannot go unprovided for."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that while these commanders are far from home, with their movements still unsettled and their families not yet settled, rumors and unrest may arise unless provision is made."

sentences.zh: 命有司安插。

translations.literal: [The throne] ordered the relevant offices to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the relevant offices to settle their families.

sentences.zh: 五年，敘來降功，授一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for merit in surrendering, he was granted the first-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, in recognition of his merit in surrendering, he was granted a first-rank jingqi niha banner rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，從英親王討大同叛將薑瓖，攻左衛，克之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Ying in campaigning against the rebel general Jiang Xiang of Datong; they attacked Zuowei and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Prince Ying in the campaign against the rebel general Jiang Xiang of Datong. They attacked Zuowei and took it.

sentences.zh: 擢本旗固山額真。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gushan ejen of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to banner commander (gushan ejen) of his own banner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封一等子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, his enfeoffment was fixed as first-rank viscount.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign his line was fixed at the rank of first-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 夢庚諸將，李國英最顯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Among Menggeng's generals, Li Guoying was the most illustrious and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Among Menggeng's commanders, Li Guoying rose highest and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 郝效忠，遼東人，隸漢軍正白旗。

translations.literal: Hao Xiaozhong, a native of Liaodong, was enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xiaozhong, a native of Liaodong, served in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 從英親王定湖南，擢湖南右路總兵，加都督僉事，授世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Following Prince Ying in pacifying Hunan, he was promoted to regional commander of the Hunan Right Route, given the additional rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military, and granted the hereditary third-rank adaha han.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Ying in pacifying Hunan and was promoted to regional commander of the Hunan Right Route. He was given the additional rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military and granted a hereditary third-rank adaha han banner rank.

sentences.zh: 孫可望陷沅州，效忠率師克黎平。

translations.literal: When Sun Kewang took Yuanzhou, Xiaozhong led his army and recovered Liping.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Kewang seized Yuanzhou, Xiaozhong led his troops and recovered Liping.

sentences.zh: 可望兵驟至，力戰，馬蹶被執，不屈，遂見殺，贈都督同知。

translations.literal: Kewang's troops arrived suddenly; [Xiaozhong] fought fiercely; his horse stumbled and he was captured; he would not submit and was therefore killed; posthumously granted Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang's army arrived suddenly. Xiaozhong fought hard until his horse stumbled and he was taken captive. He refused to yield and was put to death. He was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 徐勇，亦遼東人。

translations.literal: Xu Yong was also a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yong was also a native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 英親王檄署九江總兵，調黃州，捕治九江、黃州土寇。

translations.literal: Prince Ying appointed him by dispatch as regional commander of Jiujiang; he was transferred to Huangzhou to capture and suppress local bandits in Jiujiang and Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying appointed him acting regional commander of Jiujiang, then transferred him to Huangzhou to hunt down local bandits in the Jiujiang and Huangzhou regions.

sentences.zh: 明唐王使招之，勇斬使以聞，命移鎮長沙。

translations.literal: An envoy of the Ming Prince of Tang came to recruit him; Yong beheaded the envoy and reported it; he was ordered transferred to garrison at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy of the Ming Prince of Tang came to win him over, Yong beheaded the envoy and reported the matter. He was ordered to transfer his garrison to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛，招勇，复斬其使。

translations.literal: When Jin Shengheng rebelled, he tried to recruit Yong; [Yong] again beheaded his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengheng rebelled and tried to recruit him, Yong again beheaded the envoy.

sentences.zh: 與李錦戰江中，中矢，裹創戰愈奮。

translations.literal: He fought Li Jin on the river, was struck by an arrow, bound his wound, and fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Jin on the river, was struck by an arrow, bound his wound, and fought all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，設策守禦，錦遁去。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked the city, he devised plans for defense; Jin fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels assaulted the city, he devised a defense and drove Li Jin off.

sentences.zh: 迎鄭親王師擊破明大學士何騰蛟。

translations.literal: He welcomed Prince Zheng's army and together they defeated the Ming Grand Secretary He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Zheng's army and together they defeated the Ming Grand Secretary He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 復調辰常總兵，授世職一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to regional commander of Chen and Chang, and granted the hereditary first-rank adaha han together with the tosalaha han.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to regional commander of Chen and Chang and granted a hereditary first-rank adaha han together with a tosalaha han banner rank.

sentences.zh: 明桂王遣將張光翠、張景春窺辰州，屯荔溪。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui sent generals Zhang Guangcui and Zhang Jingchun to reconnoiter Chenzhou; they encamped at Lixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui sent generals Zhang Guangcui and Zhang Jingchun to probe Chenzhou. They encamped at Lixi.

sentences.zh: 勇督將士渡江戰，擊殺景春，擒裨將六，馘士卒數百，加左都督，進世職三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Yong led his officers and men across the river to fight; he killed Jingchun, captured six lieutenant generals, and took the heads of several hundred soldiers; he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military and advanced in hereditary rank to third-rank ashan i ha.
translations.idiomatic: Yong led his officers and men across the river to give battle. He killed Jingchun, captured six lieutenant generals, and took several hundred enemy heads. He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military and advanced in hereditary rank to third-rank ashan i ha.

sentences.zh: 桂王復遣白文選來攻，驅象為陣，破城，勇巷戰死之，贈太子太保，進世職二等，諡忠節。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui again sent Bai Wenxuan to attack; [the enemy] drove elephants into battle formation; the city was breached; Yong died fighting in the lanes; posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, advanced in hereditary rank to second rank, posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui sent Bai Wenxuan to attack again. The enemy drove war elephants into formation, breached the walls, and Yong fell fighting in the streets. He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, advanced in hereditary rank to the second rank, and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 以其兄子襲，入籍武昌衛。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son inherited; [the line] was enrolled in the Wuchang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son inherited the rank, and the family was enrolled in the Wuchang garrison.

sentences.zh: 盧光祖，遼東海州人，隸漢軍鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: Lu Guangzu, a native of Haizhou in Liaodong, was enrolled in the Bordered Blue Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangzu, a native of Haizhou in Liaodong, served in the Bordered Blue Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 從肅親王下四川，破張獻忠。

translations.literal: Following Prince Su into Sichuan, he defeated Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Su into Sichuan and defeated Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 授夔州總兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regional commander of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 擊破明桂王將硃天麟等。

translations.literal: He defeated the generals of the Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Tianlin and others.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the generals of the Ming Prince of Gui, including Zhu Tianlin.

sentences.zh: 取順慶，屢捕治土寇。

translations.literal: He took Shunqing and repeatedly captured and suppressed local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shunqing and repeatedly hunted down local bandits.

sentences.zh: 甘一爵、硃德洪據鄰水、大竹為亂。

translations.literal: Gan Yijue and Zhu Dehong held Linshui and Dazhu in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Yijue and Zhu Dehong raised rebellion from bases at Linshui and Dazhu.

sentences.zh: 光祖督師討之，戰七晝夜，斬一爵、德洪，降硐寨十餘。

translations.literal: Guangzu supervised the army in campaigning against them; they fought seven days and nights; he beheaded Yijue and Dehong and received the surrender of more than ten stockaded villages.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu led the army against them. After seven days and nights of fighting he beheaded Yijue and Dehong and received the surrender of more than ten stockaded strongholds.

sentences.zh: 以功授世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the hereditary first-rank adaha han.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted a hereditary first-rank adaha han banner rank.

sentences.zh: 孫可望破敘州，將軍李國翰率師赴援，光祖殿，遇敵，戰敗，命立功自贖。

translations.literal: When Sun Kewang took Xuzhou, General Li Guohan led troops to relieve it; Guangzu brought up the rear; he met the enemy, was defeated in battle, and was ordered to redeem himself by merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Kewang took Xuzhou, General Li Guohan marched to relieve the city. Guangzu commanded the rear guard, met the enemy, and was defeated. He was ordered to redeem himself by further service.

sentences.zh: 尋改川北總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to regional commander of North Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to regional commander of North Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓既降复叛，誅死。

translations.literal: Jin Shengheng, having surrendered, rebelled again and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shengheng, having surrendered and then rebelled again, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 田雄，直隸宣化人。

translations.literal: Tian Xiong was a native of Xuanhua in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xiong was a native of Xuanhua in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 馬得功，遼東人。

translations.literal: Ma Degong was a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Degong was a native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 仕明皆至總兵。

translations.literal: Serving the Ming, both rose to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming both rose to the rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，豫親王多鐸下江南，明福王由崧走蕪湖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when Prince Yu Dodo advanced into Jiangnan, the Ming Prince of Fu Zhu Yousong fled to Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, when Prince Yu Dodo marched into Jiangnan, the Ming Prince of Fu Zhu Yousong fled to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 巴牙喇纛章京圖賴督兵截江斷道，雄、得功縛福王及其妃來獻，豫親王令以原銜從征。

translations.literal: Baturu Duzhangjing Tulai supervised troops to block the river and cut the road; Xiong and Degong bound the Prince of Fu and his consort and brought them in submission; Prince Yu ordered them to follow the campaign with their original titles.
translations.idiomatic: Baturu banner commander Tulai led troops to block the river and cut off the route of escape. Xiong and Degong bound the Prince of Fu and his consort and presented them in submission. Prince Yu ordered both men to follow the campaign retaining their former titles.

sentences.zh: 尋授雄杭州總兵，得功鎮江總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xiong was appointed regional commander of Hangzhou and Degong regional commander of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiong was appointed regional commander of Hangzhou and Degong regional commander of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 雄佐總督張存仁、梅勒章京珠瑪喇，駐軍杭州。

translations.literal: Xiong assisted Governor Zhang Cunren and Meile Zhangjing Zhumarha, garrisoning at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong served under Governor Zhang Cunren and Meile banner commander Zhumarha, garrisoning at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時明魯王以海稱「監國」紹興，乘間渡錢塘江窺杭州，雄與存仁、珠瑪喇等屢擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai styled himself "Regent of the State" at Shaoxing; seizing an opportunity he crossed the Qiantang River to threaten Hangzhou; Xiong together with Cunren, Zhumarha, and others repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai styled himself regent of the realm at Shaoxing. Seizing an opportunity, he crossed the Qiantang River to threaten Hangzhou. Xiong, together with Cunren, Zhumarha, and others, repeatedly drove him back.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，發李成棟逆書，加左都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he uncovered Li Chengdong's treasonous letter and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he uncovered Li Chengdong's treasonous correspondence and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 八年，敘來降功，授世職一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for merit in surrendering, he was granted the hereditary first-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, in recognition of his merit in surrendering, he was granted a hereditary first-rank jingqi niha banner rank.

sentences.zh: 明魯王與其臣阮進、張名振等據舟山，雄與固山額真金礪以舟師出海擒進，遂破舟山，隳其城，名振擁魯王入海。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Lu together with his ministers Ruan Jin, Zhang Mingzhen, and others held Zhoushan; Xiong together with Gushan Ejen Jin Kan led a naval force to sea and captured Jin; they then took Zhoushan, destroyed its walls, and Mingzhen escorted the Prince of Lu out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu, together with his ministers Ruan Jin, Zhang Mingzhen, and others, held Zhoushan. Xiong and banner commander Jin Kan led a fleet to sea, captured Jin, broke Zhoushan, and razed its walls. Mingzhen then escorted the Prince of Lu out to sea.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進將阮思、陳六禦等復據舟山，朝命寧海大將軍伊爾德率師南征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the advancing generals Ruan Si, Chen Liuyu, and others again held Zhoushan; the court ordered Grand General of the Coastal Pacification Yeerde to lead troops south.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Ming generals Ruan Si, Chen Liuyu, and others seized Zhoushan again. The court ordered Grand General of Coastal Pacification Yeerde to lead an army south.

sentences.zh: 雄預治戰艦攻具，分兵遣裨將扼要隘，通聲援，而以舟師會伊爾德擊思，以橫洋、金塘為舟山要路，分兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Xiong prepared warships and siege equipment in advance, divided his forces and sent lieutenant generals to hold strategic passes, maintained communications for mutual support, and with the naval force joined Yeerde in attacking Si; taking Hengyang and Jintang as the key routes to Zhoushan, he divided troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong prepared warships and siege equipment in advance, sent lieutenant generals with detachments to hold strategic passes and keep lines of communication open, and joined Yeerde's fleet in the attack on Ruan Si. He identified Hengyang and Jintang as the key approaches to Zhoushan and sent columns to break them.

sentences.zh: 張兩翼夾擊，殲其眾無算，思赴水死。

translations.literal: He deployed both wings in a pincer attack and destroyed countless of the enemy; Si threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked from both wings in a pincer movement and destroyed the enemy by the thousands. Si threw himself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，疏請歸旗籍，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he memorialized requesting restoration to banner registration and enrollment in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he memorialized asking to be restored to banner registration and enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功兵擾浙境，陷遂安、平陽諸縣。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's troops harassed the Zhejiang border and took Suian, Pingyang, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong's forces raided the Zhejiang frontier and seized Suian, Pingyang, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾雄，上命寬之。

translations.literal: The Board of War impeached Xiong; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of War impeached Xiong, but the emperor ordered that he be treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 十六年，成功兵攻太平，擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Chenggong's troops attacked Taiping; [Xiong] drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Chenggong's army attacked Taiping, and Xiong drove it back.

sentences.zh: 復攻寧波，雄督戰，分三路進剿，成功兵引退。

translations.literal: They again attacked Ningbo; Xiong supervised the battle and advanced in three columns to suppress them; Chenggong's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they attacked Ningbo again, Xiong directed the fighting and advanced in three columns. Chenggong's forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十八年，進二等侯。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to second-rank marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to second-rank marquis.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，卒，贈太傅，諡毅勇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he died; posthumously granted Grand Tutor; posthumous title Yiyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi he died. He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Yiyong.

sentences.zh: 得功，亦隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Degong was also enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was also enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 江寧初定，明瑞昌王誼泐屯花山、龍潭間。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was first pacified, the Ming Prince of Ruichang Zhu Yile encamped between Huashan and Longtan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning was first pacified, the Ming Prince of Ruichang Zhu Yile encamped between Huashan and Longtan.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，謀攻江寧，事泄，走鎮江。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he plotted to attack Jiangning; the affair was exposed and he fled to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi he plotted an attack on Jiangning. When the plot was exposed he fled to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 得功獲誼泐，誅之。

translations.literal: Degong captured Yile and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Degong captured Yile and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 尋以收劫盜入伍，降調。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for enrolling bandits into the ranks, he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted and transferred for having enrolled bandits into his ranks.

sentences.zh: 四年，大學士洪承疇請以得功署副將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou requested that Degong be appointed acting vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou asked that Degong be appointed acting vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從浙閩總督張存仁剿建寧、邵武山寇，克松溪、政和、建陽、崇安、光澤諸縣，即令駐松溪。

translations.literal: He followed Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Zhang Cunren in suppressing mountain bandits in Jianning and Shaowu; he took Songxi, Zhenghe, Jianyang, Chong'an, Guangze, and other counties, and was then ordered to garrison at Songxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Zhang Cunren in campaigns against mountain bandits in Jianning and Shaowu, taking Songxi, Zhenghe, Jianyang, Chong'an, Guangze, and other counties. He was then ordered to garrison at Songxi.

sentences.zh: 复克慶元、永春、德化諸縣。

translations.literal: He again took Qingyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered Qingyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 六年，授右路總兵，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed regional commander of the Right Route and given the additional rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed regional commander of the Right Route and given the additional rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 克南安，破海寇林忠。

translations.literal: He took Nan'an and defeated the sea bandit Lin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He took Nan'an and defeated the pirate Lin Zhong.

sentences.zh: 复捕治興​​化、仙遊、惠安諸縣海寇鄭丹國等。

translations.literal: He again captured and suppressed the sea bandits Zheng Danguo and others in Xinghua, Xianyou, Hui'an, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also hunted down the pirates Zheng Danguo and others in Xinghua, Xianyou, Hui'an, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功據廈門。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張學聖诇成功方出，令得功攻廈門，克之。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Xuesheng learned that Chenggong was away and ordered Degong to attack Xiamen; he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Xuesheng learned that Chenggong was away and ordered Degong to attack Xiamen. Degong took the city.

sentences.zh: 成功還救，复陷。

translations.literal: Chenggong returned to relieve it and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong returned to relieve the city and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 遂圍漳州，破海澄。

translations.literal: He then besieged Zhangzhou and took Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Zhangzhou and took Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 得功退守泉州，與固山額真金礪會師解漳州圍。

translations.literal: Degong withdrew to defend Quanzhou; together with Gushan Ejen Jin Kan he united forces and lifted the siege of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Degong withdrew to defend Quanzhou. He joined banner commander Jin Kan, and together they raised the siege of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以得功初克廈門貪取財物為成功所乘，命逮治，援赦免。

translations.literal: Because Degong, when he first took Xiamen, had greedily seized goods and was thereby taken advantage of by Chenggong, he was ordered arrested and punished; he was pardoned on appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Because Degong had looted greedily when he first took Xiamen, giving Chenggong his opening, he was ordered arrested. He was pardoned on appeal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，敘前功，賜一品頂帶，出鎮泉州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, for his earlier merit, he was granted the first-rank official's hat knob and sent out to garrison Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his earlier service was recognized. He was granted the first-rank official's hat knob and sent to garrison Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 得功自陳與雄同降，援雄例乞世職，授一等精奇尼哈番，加都督同知。

translations.literal: Degong stated that he had surrendered together with Xiong, cited Xiong's precedent in requesting a hereditary office, and was granted the first-rank jingqi niha and the additional rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.
translations.idiomatic: Degong reported that he had surrendered together with Xiong and, citing Xiong's precedent, asked for a hereditary rank. He was granted a first-rank jingqi niha banner rank and the additional title of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢福建提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林忠复據永春、德化、尤溪、大田諸縣，巡撫宜永貴令得功率師討之。

translations.literal: Lin Zhong again held Yongchun, Dehua, Youxi, Datian, and other counties; Governor Yi Yonggui ordered Degong to lead troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zhong seized Yongchun, Dehua, Youxi, Datian, and other counties again. Governor Yi Yonggui ordered Degong to lead an expedition against him.

sentences.zh: 師行，寇自閩安迳攻會城，得功引師還，與城兵夾擊，圍解。

translations.literal: As the army marched out, the bandits from Min'an struck directly at the provincial capital; Degong led his troops back and, together with the garrison, attacked from both sides and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: While his army was on campaign, the rebels from Min'an struck straight at the provincial capital. Degong turned back, joined the garrison in a pincer attack, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與浙閩總督李率泰等合兵克閩安，成功屢內犯，得功擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he joined Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Li Shuaitai and others in united forces to take Min'an; Chenggong repeatedly invaded inland, and Degong drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined Zhe-Fujian Governor-General Li Shuaitai and others in taking Min'an. When Chenggong repeatedly raided inland, Degong drove him back each time.

sentences.zh: 十八年，進三等侯。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to third-rank marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to third-rank marquis.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，遷濱海居民內地，擊敗海寇阻民遷者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi coastal inhabitants were moved inland; he defeated sea bandits who obstructed the relocation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi, when coastal inhabitants were moved inland, he defeated pirates who tried to block the relocation.

sentences.zh: 二年，師進攻廈門，得功克烏沙，以舟師出海。

translations.literal: In the second year the army advanced to attack Xiamen; Degong took Wusha and put the naval force to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, as the army advanced on Xiamen, Degong took Wusha and led the fleet out to sea.

sentences.zh: 南風起，寇乘上流來戰，得功奮擊，沒於陣。

translations.literal: A south wind rose; the bandits used the upstream current to come to battle; Degong fought fiercely and perished in the engagement.
translations.idiomatic: When a south wind rose, the enemy used the current from upstream to attack. Degong fought hard and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 李率泰以聞，進一等侯，諡襄武。

translations.literal: Li Shuaitai reported it; [Degong] was advanced to first-rank marquis; posthumous title Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuaitai reported his death. Degong was advanced to first-rank marquis and given the posthumous title Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 子三奇，襲爵，官至潮州總兵。

translations.literal: His son Sanqi inherited the title and rose to regional commander of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sanqi inherited the title and eventually rose to regional commander of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，定諸侯、伯封號，雄曰順義，得功曰順勤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong the designations for marquises and earls were fixed: Xiong was called Shunyi, Degong Shunqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong the formal designations for marquises and earls were fixed: Xiong's line was called Shunyi, Degong's Shunqin.

sentences.zh: 張天祿，陝西榆林人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianlu was a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianlu was a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明季與弟天福以義勇從軍，積功至總兵。

translations.literal: In the late Ming he and his younger brother Tianfu joined the army as volunteers and through accumulated merit rose to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming he and his younger brother Tianfu entered service as volunteers and through accumulated merit both rose to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 福王時，大學士史可法督師，令屯瓜洲為前鋒。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Grand Secretary Shi Kefa served as supreme commander and ordered him to garrison at Guazhou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Grand Secretary Shi Kefa, serving as supreme commander, ordered him to garrison at Guazhou as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師下江南，天祿、天福率所部三千人從趙之龍迎降，豫親王令以原官從征，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu's army advanced into Jiangnan, Tianlu and Tianfu led their three thousand men to follow Zhao Zhilong in welcoming surrender; Prince Yu ordered them to follow the campaign with their original offices and enrolled them in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army entered Jiangnan, Tianlu and Tianfu led their three thousand men to follow Zhao Zhilong in surrendering. Prince Yu ordered them to follow the campaign with their former titles and enrolled them in the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 明僉都御史金聲家休寧，受唐王命，糾鄉勇十餘萬據徽州。

translations.literal: The Ming Censor-in-Chief Jin Sheng was a native of Xiuning; receiving orders from the Prince of Tang, he rallied more than one hundred thousand militia and held Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Censor-in-Chief Jin Sheng, a native of Xiuning, received orders from the Prince of Tang, rallied more than one hundred thousand militiamen, and seized Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 貝勒博洛遣固山額真葉臣率師擊之，天祿及總兵卜從善、李仲興、劉澤泳並從。

translations.literal: Prince Beile Bolo dispatched Gushan Ejen Echen to lead troops against him; Tianlu together with regional commanders Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, and Liu Zeyong all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Beile Bolo sent banner commander Echen at the head of an army against him. Tianlu followed together with regional commanders Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, and Liu Zeyong.

sentences.zh: 師自旌德入，戰績溪，獲聲及中軍吳國禎、副將成有功、守備萬全等，送江寧殺之。

translations.literal: The army entered from Jingde and fought at Jixi; they captured Sheng together with Central Army Commander Wu Guozhen, Vice Commander Cheng Yougong, Garrison Commander Wan Quan, and others, and sent them to Jiangning for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered from Jingde and fought at Jixi. They captured Sheng together with Central Army Commander Wu Guozhen, Vice Commander Cheng Yougong, Garrison Commander Wan Quan, and others, and sent them to Jiangning for execution.

sentences.zh: 徽州平。

translations.literal: Huizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 明大學士黃道周率兵犯徽州，天祿擊之，斬其將程嗣聖等十餘人，獲總兵李堯光等。

translations.literal: The Ming Grand Secretary Huang Daozhou led troops to attack Huizhou; Tianlu struck them, beheaded his generals Cheng Sisheng and more than ten others, and captured Regional Commander Li Yaoguang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Grand Secretary Huang Daozhou led troops against Huizhou. Tianlu attacked them, beheaded more than ten of his generals including Cheng Sisheng, and captured Regional Commander Li Yaoguang and others.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，戰婺源，獲道周，亦送江寧殺之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi they fought at Wuyuan, captured Daozhou, and likewise sent him to Jiangning for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi they fought at Wuyuan, captured Daozhou, and sent him to Jiangning for execution as well.

sentences.zh: 分兵出祁門、江灣、街口、黃源，四道逐捕道周餘眾。

translations.literal: He divided troops to go out by Qimen, Jiangwan, Jiekou, and Huangyuan—four routes—to pursue and capture Daozhou's remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns out by Qimen, Jiangwan, Jiekou, and Huangyuan—four routes—to hunt down Daozhou's remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 以功加都督同知，授徽寧池太總兵官。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military and appointed regional commander of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Military and appointed regional commander of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 天祿屯徽州城外，依山為營。

translations.literal: Tianlu encamped outside Huizhou city, building his camp against the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlu encamped outside Huizhou on the hillside.

sentences.zh: 值雨，父老迎天祿入城，天祿曰：「三軍方在泥塗，何忍獨安？」

translations.literal: When it rained, the elders welcomed Tianlu into the city; Tianlu said: "The whole army is still in the mud—how can I bear to rest alone in comfort?"
translations.idiomatic: During the rains the elders invited Tianlu into the city. Tianlu said, "The whole army is still mired in the mud—how can I alone seek comfort?"

sentences.zh: 終不下山。

translations.literal: In the end he never came down from the hill.
translations.idiomatic: He never left the hillside camp.

sentences.zh: 軍民皆稱之。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians alike praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians alike praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 明嵩安王常淇糾眾數千擾婺源，天祿率副將許漢鼎等擊之，獲常淇及監軍江於東等。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Song'an Zhu Changqi rallied several thousand men to harass Wuyuan; Tianlu led Vice Commander Xu Handing and others to attack them and captured Changqi together with Military Supervisor Jiang Yudong and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Song'an Zhu Changqi gathered several thousand men to raid Wuyuan. Tianlu led Vice Commander Xu Handing and others against them and captured Changqi together with Military Supervisor Jiang Yudong and others.

sentences.zh: 四年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 五年，敘來降功，授世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for merit in surrendering, he was granted the hereditary third-rank adaha han.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, for his merit in surrendering, he was granted a hereditary third-rank adaha han banner rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，進三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to third-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was advanced to third-rank jingqi niha.

sentences.zh: 九年，鄭成功圍漳州，命天祿赴援，成功引退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zheng Chenggong besieged Zhangzhou; Tianlu was ordered to go to the relief; Chenggong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zheng Chenggong besieged Zhangzhou. Tianlu was ordered to relieve the city, and Chenggong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天祿留駐延平，捕治山寇。

translations.literal: Tianlu remained garrisoned at Yanping to capture and suppress mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlu remained at Yanping to hunt down mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 十一年，明魯王將張名振攻崇明，天祿還松江禦戰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Ming Prince of Lu's general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming; Tianlu returned to Songjiang to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Ming Prince of Lu's general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Chongming. Tianlu returned to Songjiang to meet him in battle.

sentences.zh: 名振既出海，复侵吳淞。

translations.literal: After Mingzhen had put to sea, he again raided Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzhen had put to sea, he raided Wusong again.

sentences.zh: 我水師與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: Our naval force engaged them and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Our fleet engaged them and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 江南總督馬鳴佩劾天祿失舟師三百餘及砲械，匿未報；

translations.literal: Jiangnan Governor-General Ma Mingpei impeached Tianlu for losing more than three hundred vessels and artillery pieces and concealing the fact without reporting it;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan Governor-General Ma Mingpei impeached Tianlu for losing more than three hundred vessels and their artillery and for concealing the losses without reporting them;

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督佟泰劾天祿與名振通書：逮下刑部，讞通書無​​據，坐匿失砲械等，奪官，降世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Tong Tai impeached Tianlu for corresponding with Mingzhen: he was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Punishments; the verdict found no basis for the charge of correspondence; he was convicted of concealing the loss of artillery and the like, stripped of office, and reduced in hereditary rank to third-rank adaha han.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Tong Tai impeached him for corresponding with Mingzhen. He was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Punishments. The case found no proof of treasonous correspondence, but he was convicted of concealing the loss of the artillery and other offenses. He was stripped of office and reduced in hereditary rank to third-rank adaha han.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 天福初降，從征崑山、嘉定。

translations.literal: When Tianfu first surrendered, he followed campaigns at Kunshan and Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu first surrendered, he took part in the campaigns at Kunshan and Jiading.

sentences.zh: 民不薙發，據城抗我師，天福與總兵李成棟討平之。

translations.literal: The people would not shave their heads; they held the cities and resisted our army; Tianfu together with Regional Commander Li Chengdong suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The people refused to adopt the queue and held the cities against our forces. Tianfu and Regional Commander Li Chengdong put down the resistance.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，授陝西漢羌總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was appointed regional commander of Hanzhong and Qiang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was appointed regional commander of the Hanzhong-Qiang district in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 敘來降及戰功，授世職一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit in surrendering and in battle he was granted the hereditary first-rank ashan i ha.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in surrendering and in battle he was granted a hereditary first-rank ashan i ha banner rank.

sentences.zh: 明山陰王鼎濟聚兵據毛壩關，署單一涵為元帥。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Shanyin Wang Dingji gathered troops and held Maoba Pass, appointing Shan Yihan as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Shanyin Wang Dingji gathered troops and seized Maoba Pass, appointing Shan Yihan commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 年六，天福自漢中率師入山，獲鼎濟，一涵投崖死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Tianfu led troops from Hanzhong into the mountains, captured Dingji, and Yihan threw himself off a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Tianfu led troops from Hanzhong into the mountains, captured Dingji, and Yihan threw himself from a cliff to his death.

sentences.zh: 參將王永祥叛延安，山寇劉宏才攻同官，天福先後討平之。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Wang Yongxiang rebelled at Yan'an; the mountain bandit Liu Hongcai attacked Tongguan; Tianfu in succession suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Wang Yongxiang rebelled at Yan'an, and the mountain bandit Liu Hongcai attacked Tongguan. Tianfu put down both in turn.

sentences.zh: 以病還京師，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he returned to the capital and was appointed a minister of honorific rank.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital on grounds of illness and was appointed a minister of honorific rank.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授本旗都統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed commander-in-chief of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed commander-in-chief of his banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kangxi he died.

sentences.zh: 趙之龍，江南虹縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhilong was a native of Hong County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhilong was a native of Hong County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，以忻城伯鎮南京。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he garrisoned Nanjing as Marquis of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he held Nanjing as Marquis of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 福王立，與擁戴，干政。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he took part in raising him and meddled in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he had helped raise him to the throne and meddled in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 豫親王師至，與魏國公徐允爵，保國公張國弼，隆平侯張拱日，臨淮侯李祖述，懷寧侯孫維城，靈壁侯湯國祚，安遠侯柳祚昌，永昌侯徐宏爵，定遠侯鄧文囿，項城伯常應俊，大興伯鄒存義，寧晉伯劉允極，南和伯方一元，東寧伯焦夢熊，安城伯張國才，洛中伯黃九鼎，成安伯郭祚永，駙馬齊贊元，大學士王鐸，尚書錢謙益，侍郎硃之臣、梁雲構、李綽等迎降。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu's army arrived, he together with the Duke of Wei Xu Yunjue, the Duke of Bao Zhang Guobi, the Marquis of Longping Zhang Gongri, the Marquis of Linhuai Li Zushu, the Marquis of Huaining Sun Weicheng, the Marquis of Lingbi Tang Guozuo, the Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang, the Marquis of Yongchang Xu Hongjue, the Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenyou, the Earl of Xiangcheng Chang Yingjun, the Earl of Daxing Zou Cunyi, the Earl of Ningjin Liu Yunji, the Earl of Nanhe Fang Yiyuan, the Earl of Dongning Jiao Mengxiong, the Earl of Ancheng Zhang Guocai, the Earl of Luozhong Huang Jiuding, the Earl of Cheng'an Guo Zuoyong, the imperial son-in-law Qi Zanyuan, Grand Secretary Wang Duo, Minister Qian Qianyi, Vice Ministers Zhu Zhichen, Liang Yungou, Li Chuo, and others welcomed surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu's army arrived, Zhilong joined the Duke of Wei Xu Yunjue, the Duke of Bao Zhang Guobi, the Marquis of Longping Zhang Gongri, the Marquis of Linhuai Li Zushu, the Marquis of Huaining Sun Weicheng, the Marquis of Lingbi Tang Guozuo, the Marquis of Anyuan Liu Zuochang, the Marquis of Yongchang Xu Hongjue, the Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenyou, the Earl of Xiangcheng Chang Yingjun, the Earl of Daxing Zou Cunyi, the Earl of Ningjin Liu Yunji, the Earl of Nanhe Fang Yiyuan, the Earl of Dongning Jiao Mengxiong, the Earl of Ancheng Zhang Guocai, the Earl of Luozhong Huang Jiuding, the Earl of Cheng'an Guo Zuoyong, the imperial son-in-law Qi Zanyuan, Grand Secretary Wang Duo, Minister Qian Qianyi, Vice Ministers Zhu Zhichen, Liang Yungou, Li Chuo, and others in welcoming the Qing forces and surrendering.

sentences.zh: 之龍授世職三等阿思哈尼哈番，允爵等皆置勿用。

translations.literal: Zhilong was granted the hereditary third-rank ashan i ha; Yunjue and the others were all set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong was granted a hereditary third-rank ashan i ha banner rank. Yunjue and the other nobles were set aside and not employed.

sentences.zh: 鐸等詣京師。

translations.literal: Duo and the others went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Duo and the others went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是北都降者多授原官，御史盧傳言南都新人不得與舊臣比。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who surrendered at the Northern Capital were mostly given their original offices; Censor Lu Chuan said that newcomers from the Southern Capital could not be compared with old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, most of those who surrendered at the Northern Capital had been given their former offices. Censor Lu Chuan argued that newcomers from the Southern Capital could not be treated on the same footing as long-serving ministers of the earlier surrender.

sentences.zh: 鐸至，命以尚書管弘文院學士，累擢至禮部尚書，卒，諡文安。

translations.literal: When Duo arrived, he was ordered to serve as Minister directing the Hanlin Academy of Hongwen; he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites; he died; posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo arrived, he was appointed Minister in charge of the Hongwen Academy. He rose eventually to Minister of Rites, died, and was given the posthumous title Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 謙益語在文苑傳。

translations.literal: Qianyi's account is in the literary biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi's account appears in the literary biographies.

sentences.zh: 孫可望，陝西延長人。

translations.literal: Sun Kewang was a native of Yanchang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang was a native of Yanchang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 從張獻忠為賊，與李定國、劉文秀、艾能奇並為獻忠養子。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Xianzhong as a bandit; together with Li Dingguo, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi he was adopted as Xianzhong's son.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Xianzhong in rebellion, and together with Li Dingguo, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi was adopted as Xianzhong's son.

sentences.zh: 獻忠據四川，使分將其眾，可望號平東將軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong held Sichuan, he had them each command part of his forces; Kewang styled himself General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong held Sichuan, he had them each command a portion of his forces. Kewang styled himself General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，肅親王豪格師定四川，獻忠敗死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Prince Su Haoge's army pacified Sichuan; Xianzhong was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, Prince Su Haoge's army pacified Sichuan. Xianzhong was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 可望與定國等率殘眾南竄，道重慶、綦江、遵義入貴陽。

translations.literal: Kewang together with Dingguo and the others led the remnant forces south in flight, passing through Chongqing, Qijiang, and Zunyi to enter Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang, Dingguo, and the others led the remnant forces south through Chongqing, Qijiang, and Zunyi into Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 阿迷土司沙定洲亂雲南，可望率眾兼程赴之。

translations.literal: The Ami chieftain Sha Dingzhou raised rebellion in Yunnan; Kewang led his followers day and night to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: The Ami chieftain Sha Dingzhou rebelled in Yunnan. Kewang marched his forces day and night to reach the province.

sentences.zh: 定洲方攻楚雄，迎戰大敗，走歸阿迷。

translations.literal: Dingzhou was then attacking Chuxiong; he met them in battle and was greatly defeated, fleeing back to Ami.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou was then besieging Chuxiong. He met Kewang in battle, suffered a crushing defeat, and fled back to Ami.

sentences.zh: 可望入雲南會城，遣定國徇迤東，而與文秀率兵西出，得副使楊畏知，相誓扶明室，與俱至楚雄，略迤西諸府。

translations.literal: Kewang entered the Yunnan provincial capital, sent Dingguo to campaign in the eastern circuit, and himself with Wenxiu led troops west; he obtained Vice Commissioner Yang Weizhi; they swore together to support the Ming house; together they reached Chuxiong and subdued the prefectures of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang entered the Yunnan provincial capital, sent Dingguo to secure the eastern circuit, and marched west with Wenxiu. He won over Vice Commissioner Yang Weizhi, and together they swore to restore the Ming. They advanced to Chuxiong and subdued the prefectures of the western circuit.

sentences.zh: 定國亦定迤東諸府。

translations.literal: Dingguo also pacified the prefectures of the eastern circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo likewise pacified the prefectures of the eastern circuit.

sentences.zh: 可望遂盡有雲南，自號平東王，以乾支紀年，鑄錢曰「興朝通寶」。

translations.literal: Kewang then came to hold all of Yunnan; he styled himself Prince Who Pacifies the East, reckoned years by the sexagenary cycle, and cast coin reading "Xingchao Tongbao."
translations.idiomatic: Kewang then held all of Yunnan. He styled himself Prince Who Pacifies the East, dated his reign by the sexagenary cycle, and cast coins inscribed "Xingchao Tongbao."

sentences.zh: 時能奇已前死，可望並將其眾。

translations.literal: By then Nengqi had already died earlier; Kewang also took command of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Nengqi had already died by then, and Kewang absorbed his forces as well.

sentences.zh: 定國、文秀故等夷，不為可望下。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu had originally been his equals and would not submit to Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu had originally been his equals and would not bow to Kewang.

sentences.zh: 可望假事杖定國，欲以威眾，隙益深。

translations.literal: Kewang used a pretext to have Dingguo beaten with the staff, intending thereby to awe the multitude; the rift grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang used a pretext to have Dingguo beaten with the staff, hoping to intimidate the others. The breach between them only deepened.

sentences.zh: 明桂王在肇慶，乃遣畏知奉表乞王封，桂王封可望景國公，賜名朝宗。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui was at Zhaoqing; [Kewang] then sent Weizhi to present a memorial requesting princely enfeoffment; the Prince of Gui enfeoffed Kewang as Duke of Jing and bestowed the name Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui was at Zhaoqing. Kewang sent Weizhi to present a memorial requesting a princely title. The Prince of Gui enfeoffed Kewang as Duke of Jing and bestowed the name Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 使以敕印往，而桂王諸將爭欲得可望為強援。

translations.literal: The envoy was sent with the edict and seal, but the Prince of Gui's generals each contended to win Kewang as a powerful ally.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was dispatched with the edict and seal, but the Prince of Gui's generals each sought to win Kewang as a powerful ally.

sentences.zh: 堵胤錫駐梧州，承製改封平遼王；

translations.literal: Du Yinxie was garrisoned at Wuzhou and, acting on imperial authority, changed the enfeoffment to Prince Who Pacifies Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: Du Yinxie, garrisoned at Wuzhou, acting on his own authority changed the title to Prince Who Pacifies Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 陳邦傅守泗城，又矯命封秦王；

translations.literal: Chen Bangfu held Sicheng and again forged an order enfeoffing him as Prince of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bangfu, holding Sicheng, forged another order enfeoffing him as Prince of Qin;

sentences.zh: 可望乃不受景國公命。

translations.literal: Kewang therefore did not accept the command as Duke of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang therefore refused to accept the title of Duke of Jing.

sentences.zh: 會我師克韶州，桂王走梧州。

translations.literal: Just then our army took Shaozhou and the Prince of Gui fled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When our army took Shaozhou, the Prince of Gui fled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 可望復遣使請封，議封澂江王。

translations.literal: Kewang again sent envoys requesting enfeoffment; it was proposed to enfeoff him as Prince of Chengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent envoys again to request a title. The court debated enfeoffing him as Prince of Chengjiang.

sentences.zh: 使者謂非秦不敢復命，大學士嚴起恆持不可，議中寢。

translations.literal: The envoy said that unless he were made Prince of Qin he dared not return with his report; Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng held that this could not be allowed, and the deliberation was dropped midway.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy declared that unless Kewang were made Prince of Qin he dared not return. Grand Secretary Yan Qiheng objected, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 可望襲貴陽，復遣文秀攻嘉定，入四川。

translations.literal: Kewang raided Guiyang and again sent Wenxiu to attack Jiading and enter Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang raided Guiyang and again sent Wenxiu to attack Jiading and advance into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 我師定兩廣，桂王至南寧，乃遣使封可望冀王，可望猶不受，復使畏知詣桂王，而遣其將賀九儀等以五千人先驅，取起恆及諸臣阻秦封者盡殺之。

translations.literal: Our army pacified the two Guang provinces; the Prince of Gui reached Nanning and then sent envoys to enfeoff Kewang as Prince of Ji; Kewang still would not accept; he again sent Weizhi to the Prince of Gui, while dispatching his generals He Jiuyi and others with five thousand men as vanguard to seize Yan Qiheng and all the ministers who had opposed the Qin enfeoffment and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: After our army pacified the two Guang provinces, the Prince of Gui reached Nanning and sent envoys to enfeoff Kewang as Prince of Ji. Kewang still refused. He sent Weizhi to the Prince of Gui again, while dispatching his generals He Jiuyi and others with five thousand men ahead to seize Yan Qiheng and all the ministers who had blocked the Qin enfeoffment and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 桂王乃真封可望秦王，而留畏知授大學士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui then truly enfeoffed Kewang as Prince of Qin, while retaining Weizhi and appointing him Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui then formally enfeoffed Kewang as Prince of Qin and retained Weizhi, appointing him Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 可望聞之怒，召至貴陽面數之，畏知以冠擊可望，亦被殺。

translations.literal: When Kewang heard of this he was enraged; he summoned [Weizhi] to Guiyang and rebuked him to his face; Weizhi struck Kewang with his hat and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang heard of this he was furious. He summoned Weizhi to Guiyang and rebuked him to his face. Weizhi struck Kewang with his official cap and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 桂王遣大學士文安之督師四川，將以招川中諸鎮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui dispatched Grand Secretary Wen Anzhi to serve as supreme commander in Sichuan, intending thereby to win over the various garrisons in the province.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui sent Grand Secretary Wen Anzhi to Sichuan as supreme commander, hoping to win over the garrisons there.

sentences.zh: 可望遣兵伺於都勻，邀止之。

translations.literal: Kewang sent troops to lie in wait at Duyun and intercepted and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent troops to lie in wait at Duyun and turned him back.

sentences.zh: 可望將移桂王自近，挾以作威。

translations.literal: Kewang intended to move the Prince of Gui close at hand and use him to assert his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang planned to bring the Prince of Gui close at hand and use him to assert his own authority.

sentences.zh: 桂王奔廣南，可望遣兵迎入安隆所，改為安龍府，歲供銀八千、米百石，窮迫不可堪；

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui fled to Guangnan; Kewang sent troops to welcome him into Anlong Subprefecture, which was changed to Anlong Prefecture; each year eight thousand taels of silver and one hundred piculs of grain were supplied—he was reduced to such straits as could not be endured;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui fled to Guangnan. Kewang sent troops to bring him into Anlong Subprefecture, which was renamed Anlong Prefecture. He was allotted eight thousand taels of silver and one hundred piculs of grain a year—a poverty so grinding it was unbearable;

sentences.zh: 而馬吉祥、龐天壽輩方欲戴可望行禪讓，可望遂自設內閣六部等官，立太廟，定朝儀，改印文為八疊。

translations.literal: while Ma Jixiang, Pang Tianshou, and their faction wished to place the imperial cap on Kewang and have him receive the abdication; Kewang therefore set up on his own the Grand Secretariat, the Six Ministries, and other offices, established the Imperial Ancestral Temple, fixed court ritual, and changed official seals to eight folds.
translations.idiomatic: while Ma Jixiang, Pang Tianshou, and their faction wished to place the imperial crown on Kewang through a ritual abdication. Kewang therefore established his own Grand Secretariat, Six Ministries, and other offices, founded an imperial ancestral temple, fixed court ritual, and changed official seals to the eight-fold style.

sentences.zh: 桂王益憂懼。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui grew still more anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui grew ever more anxious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 初，定國自廣西入湖廣，兵益強，不復禀可望約束。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dingguo had entered Huguang from Guangxi; his army grew ever stronger and he no longer reported to or obeyed Kewang's constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dingguo had marched from Guangxi into Huguang. His army grew stronger and he no longer submitted to Kewang's authority.

sentences.zh: 會定國敗於衡州，使召詣沅州議事，將以為罪而殺之；

translations.literal: When Dingguo was defeated at Hengzhou, [Kewang] sent to summon him to Yuanzhou to discuss affairs, intending to find him guilty and kill him;
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo was defeated at Hengzhou, Kewang summoned him to Yuanzhou on the pretext of consultation, intending to condemn and kill him;

sentences.zh: 定國辭不赴，又自柳州攻肇慶，下高、廉、雷諸府。

translations.literal: Dingguo declined and did not go; he again from Liuzhou attacked Zhaoqing and took the prefectures of Gao, Lian, and Lei.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo refused to come. From Liuzhou he attacked Zhaoqing again and took the prefectures of Gao, Lian, and Lei.

sentences.zh: 至是，桂王聞定國兵強，密詔使入衛。

translations.literal: By this time the Prince of Gui, hearing that Dingguo's army was strong, secretly issued an edict summoning him to come and guard the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Gui, hearing how strong Dingguo's army had become, secretly ordered him to come and guard the court.

sentences.zh: 可望聞，使執大學士吳貞毓等，凡預謀者盡殺之。

translations.literal: When Kewang heard of it, he had Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others arrested; all who had taken part in the plot were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang learned of this, he arrested Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others. Everyone involved in the plot was put to death.

sentences.zh: 議移桂王貴陽，使其將白文選督行期。

translations.literal: It was proposed to move the Prince of Gui to Guiyang; his general Bai Wenxuan was ordered to supervise the date of departure.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to move the Prince of Gui to Guiyang and ordered his general Bai Wenxuan to supervise the move.

sentences.zh: 文選心不直可望，以情輸桂王，緩其行。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's heart was not loyal to Kewang; he confided the situation to the Prince of Gui and delayed the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was not loyal to Kewang. He confided in the Prince of Gui and delayed the move.

sentences.zh: 俟定國至，奉桂王自安南衛走雲南。

translations.literal: They waited until Dingguo arrived, then escorted the Prince of Gui from Annan Guard to flee to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: They waited until Dingguo arrived, then escorted the Prince of Gui from Annan Guard into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時文秀守雲南，亦怨可望，迎桂王入雲南會城。

translations.literal: At that time Wenxiu was defending Yunnan and also resented Kewang; he welcomed the Prince of Gui into the Yunnan provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu was then defending Yunnan and also resented Kewang. He welcomed the Prince of Gui into the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 可望舉兵反桂王，以雙禮留守，令文選統諸軍前行。

translations.literal: Kewang raised troops in rebellion against the Prince of Gui; he left Shuangli to hold the rear and ordered Wenxuan to command the various armies in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang raised an army against the Prince of Gui. He left Shuangli to hold the rear and ordered Wenxuan to lead the advance.

sentences.zh: 定國、文秀率師御之，次三岔河，夾水而軍。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu led troops to resist them; they halted at Sancha River and encamped on opposite banks.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu marched to meet them and halted at Sancha River, encamping on opposite banks.

sentences.zh: 文選輕騎奔定國。

translations.literal: Wenxuan with a light cavalry detachment galloped to Dingguo's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan rode with a light detachment to join Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 可望遣其將張勝、馬寶等自尋甸間道襲雲南，而自率勁卒擊定國等。

translations.literal: Kewang dispatched his generals Zhang Sheng, Ma Bao, and others by a secret route from Xundian to raid Yunnan, while he himself led crack troops to attack Dingguo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent his generals Zhang Sheng and Ma Bao by a hidden route from Xundian to strike Yunnan, while he himself led elite troops against Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 戰方合，其將馬惟興先奔，遂大潰，定國遣文秀等追之。

translations.literal: Just as battle was joined, his general Ma Weixing fled first; the army then collapsed in great disorder; Dingguo sent Wenxiu and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was joined, his general Ma Weixing fled first. The army collapsed in rout, and Dingguo sent Wenxiu and others in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 可望至貴陽，雙禮紿言追兵且至。

translations.literal: When Kewang reached Guiyang, Shuangli deceived him, saying that pursuing troops were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang reached Guiyang, Shuangli deceived him with word that pursuers were close behind.

sentences.zh: 可望知事去，將詣經略洪承疇請降，遣使先納款。

translations.literal: Kewang knew the affair was lost; he was about to go to Frontier Commissioner Hong Chengchou to request surrender and sent envoys ahead to tender allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang knew all was lost. He prepared to go to Frontier Commissioner Hong Chengchou to surrender and sent envoys ahead to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 文秀等遣將楊武追之，及於沙子嶺。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and the others sent the general Yang Wu in pursuit; he caught up with him at Shaziling.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu and the others sent General Yang Wu in pursuit. Yang caught up with him at Shaziling.

sentences.zh: 承疇援兵至，乃得脫，將妻子詣長沙降，時順治十四年十月也。

translations.literal: When Chengchou's relief troops arrived, [Kewang] was able to escape; he brought his wife and children to Changsha to surrender—it was the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengchou's relief troops arrived, Kewang escaped. He brought his wife and children to Changsha to surrender in the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 詔封義王，慰諭之。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Yi and comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Yi and offered words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 尋遣學士麻勒吉等齎敕印冊封。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Academician Mele and others were dispatched bearing the edict, seal, and investiture documents.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Academician Mele and others were sent with the edict, seal, and patent of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詣京師，命簡親王濟度等郊迎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went to the capital; Prince Jian Jidu and others were ordered to welcome him in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he went to the capital. Prince Jian Jidu and others were ordered to welcome him beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 入覲，宴中和殿，賜白金萬，官其部將陳杰，劉天瑞等百餘人，命隸漢軍正白旗。

translations.literal: He came to audience; a banquet was held in the Hall of Central Harmony; ten thousand taels of white silver were granted; more than one hundred of his subordinate generals, including Chen Jie and Liu Tianrui, were given offices and ordered enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: He had an audience and was feasted in the Hall of Central Harmony. He was granted ten thousand taels of silver. More than one hundred of his subordinate commanders, including Chen Jie and Liu Tianrui, were given offices and enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 可望請從討雲南自效，下王大臣議，寢其奏。

translations.literal: Kewang requested to follow in the campaign against Yunnan to prove his merit; the memorial was sent down to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation and was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang asked to join the campaign against Yunnan to prove his loyalty. The memorial was referred to the princes and grand ministers and set aside.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏辭封爵，复慰諭之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized declining his enfeoffment and rank; he was again comforted and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized declining his title and rank. The throne again reassured him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，諡恪順。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; posthumous title Keshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was given the posthumous title Keshun.

sentences.zh: 子徵淇襲，未幾卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhengqi inherited; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengqi inherited the title but died before long.

sentences.zh: 徵淳襲，卒，諡順愍。

translations.literal: Zhengchun inherited; he died; posthumous title Shunmin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun inherited, then died and was given the posthumous title Shunmin.

sentences.zh: 徵灝請襲，御史孟飛熊疏言：「可望，獻忠餘黨，久據滇、黔，負固不服。
