translations.literal: Zhenghao requested to inherit; Censor Meng Feixiong memorialized: "Kewang was a remnant follower of Xianzhong who long held Yunnan and Guizhou and stubbornly refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghao asked to inherit. Censor Meng Feixiong memorialized: "Kewang was a remnant of Xianzhong's band who long held Yunnan and Guizhou and stubbornly refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 及為定國所敗，窮蹙來歸，濫膺非分。

translations.literal: Only when defeated by Dingguo, reduced to extremity, did he come to submit, and he was lavished with honors beyond his due.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Dingguo defeated him and he was driven to extremity did he come over, yet he was showered with honors beyond his deserts.

sentences.zh: 宜即停止，或以次降等。」

translations.literal: The succession should be stopped at once, or the rank reduced by one degree."
translations.idiomatic: The succession should be stopped at once, or the rank reduced by one degree."

sentences.zh: 下部議，降襲慕義公，官至兵部尚書，諡清端。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the relevant ministry for deliberation; inheritance was reduced to Duke of Muyi; [Zhenghao] rose to Minister of War; posthumous title Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries. The line was reduced to Duke of Muyi. Zhenghao rose to Minister of War and was given the posthumous title Qingduan.

sentences.zh: 子降襲一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: His son Jiang inherited the first-rank adaha han.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang inherited a first-rank adaha han banner rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，命停襲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong an order was issued to stop the inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong an order ended the succession.

sentences.zh: 文選，陝西吳堡人，亦從獻忠為賊。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, a native of Wubao in Shaanxi, also followed Xianzhong as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, a native of Wubao in Shaanxi, had also followed Xianzhong in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 獻忠敗，從可望入貴州。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong was defeated, he followed Kewang into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong was defeated, he followed Kewang into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其緩桂王使得入雲南也，桂王封為鞏國公，令還貴陽慰諭可望，可望奪其兵，置軍中。

translations.literal: In delaying the Prince of Gui so that he could enter Yunnan, the Prince of Gui enfeoffed him as Duke of Gong and ordered him to return to Guiyang to comfort and instruct Kewang; Kewang stripped him of his troops and placed him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: For delaying the move so the Prince of Gui could reach Yunnan, the Prince of Gui enfeoffed him as Duke of Gong and ordered him back to Guiyang to reassure Kewang. Kewang stripped him of his command and kept him in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 及將舉兵，諸將說可望原得文選為大將，可望使將前鋒，遂降定國，可望以是敗。

translations.literal: When [Kewang] was about to raise troops, the generals urged that he ought to have Wenxuan as grand commander; Kewang had him lead the vanguard; [Wenxuan] then surrendered to Dingguo; Kewang was thereby defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Kewang was about to march, his generals urged that he should have Wenxuan as commander. Kewang made him lead the vanguard. Wenxuan then went over to Dingguo, and that was how Kewang was defeated.

sentences.zh: 桂王封文選鞏昌王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui enfeoffed Wenxuan as Prince of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui enfeoffed Wenxuan as Prince of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，我師下雲南，定國戰屢敗，令文選為殿；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi our army advanced into Yunnan; Dingguo was repeatedly defeated in battle and ordered Wenxuan to bring up the rear;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi our army entered Yunnan. Dingguo suffered repeated defeats and ordered Wenxuan to cover the retreat;

sentences.zh: 戰於玉龍關，文選复敗，走木邦。

translations.literal: They fought at Yulong Pass; Wenxuan was again defeated and fled to Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: At Yulong Pass Wenxuan was defeated again and fled to Mubang.

sentences.zh: 桂王入緬甸，居赭硜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui entered Burma and dwelt at Zhe'e.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gui entered Burma and lived at Zhe'e.

sentences.zh: 十七年，文選攻阿瓦，弗克，與定國會師孟艮；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Wenxuan attacked Ava but could not take it; he joined Dingguo at Menggen;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Wenxuan attacked Ava without success and joined Dingguo at Menggen;

sentences.zh: 再攻阿瓦，求出桂王，終不獲，我師益深入。

translations.literal: they attacked Ava again, seeking to bring out the Prince of Gui, but in the end could not obtain him; our army pressed ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Ava again to recover the Prince of Gui but failed. Our army pressed ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 文選據錫箔，憑江拒守。

translations.literal: Wenxuan held Xibo and relied on the river to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan held Xibo and defended the river line.

sentences.zh: 我師出木邦，造筏將渡，文選奔茶山。

translations.literal: Our army came out from Mubang, built rafts intending to cross; Wenxuan fled to Chashan.
translations.idiomatic: Our army advanced from Mubang and built rafts to cross the river. Wenxuan fled to Chashan.

sentences.zh: 總兵馬寧將偏師追之，及於猛養，文選降。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ma Ning led a detached force in pursuit and caught up with him at Mengyang; Wenxuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ma Ning led a detached force in pursuit and caught him at Mengyang. Wenxuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔封承恩公，亦隸漢軍正白旗。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as Duke of Chengen; he was also enrolled in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as Duke of Chengen and enrolled him in the Plain White Banner of the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，命予三等公俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was ordered granted the salary of a third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was granted the salary of a third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 七年，加太子少師。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子繪，降襲一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited at a reduced rank the first-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited at a reduced rank a first-rank jingqi niha banner title.

sentences.zh: 卒，停襲。

translations.literal: He died; the inheritance was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and the succession ended.

sentences.zh: 論曰：邦家新造，師行所至，逆者誅，順者庸。

translations.literal: The commentators say: When the state is newly founded, wherever the army marches, those who resist are punished and those who submit are rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When a dynasty is newly founded, wherever the army marches, those who resist are punished and those who submit are rewarded.

sentences.zh: 雖其人叛故國，賊舊君，苟為利於我，固不能不以為功也。

translations.literal: Even if a man has betrayed his former state and wronged his former sovereign, so long as he is useful to us, he cannot but be counted meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Even men who betrayed their former state and wronged their former sovereign could not but be counted meritorious if they served the new dynasty's interest.

sentences.zh: 可望獨以台官言降爵，終見削奪。

translations.literal: Kewang alone, on the censor's words, had his rank reduced, and in the end saw it stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang alone, on a censor's memorial, had his rank reduced and in the end saw the line stripped away entirely.

sentences.zh: 唐通降自成，既復來歸，授世職，康熙間即停襲，事又在其前；

translations.literal: Tang Tong surrendered to Zicheng, then came back again and was granted a hereditary office; in the Kangxi reign the inheritance was already stopped—this affair came even earlier;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Tong had surrendered to Li Zicheng, then returned and was granted a hereditary rank, yet even his line was ended in the Kangxi reign—an earlier case still;

sentences.zh: 而定國、夢庚、雄輩及他諸降將，皆襲封如故。

translations.literal: yet Dingguo, Menggeng, Xiong, and the other surrendered generals all inherited their enfeoffments as before.
translations.idiomatic: yet Dingguo, Menggeng, Xiong, and the other surrendered commanders kept their hereditary titles without such reduction.

sentences.zh: 民間傳雄負福王出，王咬其項，遂潰死。

translations.literal: Among the people it is said that when Xiong carried the Prince of Fu out, the prince bit his neck and he thereupon collapsed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Popular legend says that when Xiong was escorting the Prince of Fu away, the prince bit his neck and he collapsed and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 雄死時，明亡已二十年。

translations.literal: When Xiong died, the Ming had already perished twenty years before.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong died, the Ming had already fallen twenty years earlier.

sentences.zh: 其言誠無稽，然民之所惡，蓋亦可見矣。

translations.literal: The tale is truly without basis, yet what the people detest may also be seen therein.
translations.idiomatic: The tale has no historical basis, yet it shows how deeply the people detested him.
